This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse sine,

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have $4{x}^{2}=(2x)^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=2x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-4{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(2x)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\cdot (\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(2x)}{2}+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int \frac{\frac{1}{5}}{\sqrt{1 - 25 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Use the linear substitution $u=5 x.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=5,\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\frac{1}{5})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{1}{5}}{\sqrt{1 - 25 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(5 x)^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{1}{5}(\frac{1}{5})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{1}{25}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{25}+C \\  &= \frac{\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(5 x \right)}}{25}+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\sqrt{25 - 5 x^{2}}=\sqrt{25(1-(\frac{1}{5})x^{2})}
$$

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=(\sqrt{5})\,\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Apply the basic inverse-trigonometric integral:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}& \int \frac{\frac{7}{4}}{\sqrt{25 - 5 x^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{7}{20}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(\frac{\sqrt{5} x}{5})^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}x \\  &= \frac{7}{20}(\sqrt{5})\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7 \sqrt{5}}{20}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-u^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}u \\  &= \frac{7 \sqrt{5} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(u \right)}}{20}+C \\  &= \frac{7 \sqrt{5} \operatorname{arcsin}{\left(\frac{\sqrt{5} x}{5} \right)}}{20}+C\end{aligned}
